questions.question: Is magnesium a toxic heavy metal or a nutrient?
questions.answer: Magnesium is a nutritionally essential metal and an enzyme cofactor, so it is primarily a nutrient rather than a purely toxic heavy metal. According to [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]], deficiency is usually more clinically important than excess, though high exposure can still cause harm.

questions.question: Can you get too much magnesium, and what happens if you do?
questions.answer: Yes. While magnesium deficiency is usually the more clinically important concern, [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]] notes that high magnesium exposure can produce neuromuscular, cardiovascular, and central nervous system toxicity.

questions.question: Why does the Heavy Metal Index have so little detailed information on magnesium?
questions.answer: This magnesium page is currently a source-map stub created during the re-ingest of [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]]. Substantive magnesium-specific detail awaits a dedicated magnesium ingest, so the page reflects only that one source for now.

questions.question: What role does magnesium play in the body?
questions.answer: Magnesium functions as a nutritionally essential metal and an enzyme cofactor, per [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]]. The page frames it as an essential-metal node where the primary clinical concern is deficiency rather than excess.
